metadata.title: MARKETS LIVE: Nasdaq closes down 748 points as AI selloff rattles Wall Street

content.text:
1:20pm: Intel plunges
Intel Corp (NASDAQ:INTC, XETRA:INL) was on track for its worst single-day decline since 1974, as a weaker-than-expected outlook raised concerns about slowing PC demand and production constraints.
The sell-off came despite Intel reporting stronger-than-expected third-quarter results, with revenue of US$16.5 billion, gross margins of 44.1% and adjusted earnings per share of US$0.52, beating its guidance.
The company's data center and AI business provided much of the upside, with revenue rising 17% sequentially to US$7.3 billion, up around 78% year over year. Management expects the division to grow at a mid-teens rate in the fourth quarter, reflecting strong demand for server processors as AI infrastructure investment expands.
However, that strength was overshadowed by weakness in the client computing business, where revenue fell 9% sequentially to US$8.1 billion.
Higher memory prices are weighing on PC affordability, while manufacturers are reducing inventories. Intel now expects PC shipments to decline around 12% in 2026 and a further 10% in 2027, according to analyst commentary.
12:15pm: FTSE level
London's FTSE 100 escaped the chaos on Wall Street Friday, finishing flat at 10,723 points.
"An initial rally—driven by blockbuster quarterly earnings from AstraZeneca and BP, paired with continued relief over Chancellor John Healey's less punitive budget tax measures—gradually faded as sharp declines across domestic banking heavyweights and mining stocks weighed on sentiment," noted Tickmill's Patrick Munnelly.
"Despite the late-session pullback, the blue-chip index successfully locked in its first positive monthly performance in three months."
11:10am: Crypto stocks bleed
Cryptocurrency-related stocks tumbled on Friday after Binance disclosed a security breach with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, potentially the largest crypto theft on record.
Coinbase Global Inc (NASDAQ:COIN) (Coinbase Global Inc (NASDAQ:COIN)) shares fell 13%, while Robinhood Markets Inc (NASDAQ:HOOD) (Robinhood Markets Inc (NASDAQ:HOOD)) dropped 8%. Circle Internet Group (NYSE:CRCL) lost 8.5%, and MicroStrategy Incorporated (NASDAQ:MSTR) (MicroStrategy Incorporated (NASDAQ:MSTR)), the largest publicly traded corporate holder of Bitcoin, declined 8%.
The breach at the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange has raised fresh concerns about security across the digital asset industry, even as Binance said customer funds remained safe.
Binance's initial investigation indicated that an attacker may have gained access through a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer, allowing unauthorized withdrawal transactions to be submitted through a service container.
10:00 am ET: Wall Street opens down
The Nasdaq opened at its lowest level in more than two months on Friday as Amazon's aggressive AI spending plans and Intel's warning of cash burn heightened concerns about the rising cost of AI infrastructure and the time needed to generate returns.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 41.3p, or 0.08%, to 52,383.90 at the open, while the S&P 500 fell 89.3p, or 1.16%, to 7,631.07.
The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 592.2p, or 2.26%, to 25,592.486, extending its losses as investors reassessed the outlook for AI-related stocks.
Added to this mix was the US equity funds recording their first weekly net outflows in three weeks as investors turned cautious ahead of earnings from major AI companies, amid growing concerns about the escalating cost of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, according to Reuters.
Investors withdrew a net $6.65 billion from US equity funds in the week ended 28 October, the first weekly outflow since 7 October, data from LSEG Lipper showed.
The fund outflows coincided with disappointing reactions to Alphabet and Amazon's result, and could add to today's market volitality.
Intel shares plunged 26.8% to $67.38 in Friday morning trading after the chipmaker issued disappointing fourth-quarter revenue and earnings guidance following Thursday's close, overshadowing an otherwise strong third-quarter performance and triggering a sharp sell-off.
Alphabet's class A shares fell 1.01% to $280.96 in early trading.
Shares in ExxonMobil rose 1.94% to $186.85, while Chevron gained 1.37% to $234.62, as investors welcomed stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings from both US oil majors.
ExxonMobil reported adjusted earnings of $17.5 billion, beating analysts' $16.6 billion estimate, as surging refining margins lifted profits from its fuel-making business.
Chevron reported adjusted earnings of $10.4 billion, supported by record crude throughput at its US refineries, which operated at 98% utilisation.
The cryptocurrency market is showing a broad sell-off following reports that hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts described as potentially the biggest financial heist in history, blaming North Korea for the attack.
Cryptocurrency prices fell following the news, while Binance suspended withdrawals and pledged to cover the losses using its own funds.
Stablecoin issuers, including El Salvador-based Tether and Trump-backed World Liberty Financial, froze about half of the stolen assets.
At 9:33 am ET, Bitcoin had fallen 4.04% to $76,963, reflecting growing caution among investors.
Ethereum was down 4.67%, while Solana had lost 5.15%.
The FTSE 100 edged higher on Friday afternoon, putting the blue-chip index on track for its first monthly gain in three months.
At 1:49 pm GMT, the FTSE 100 was trading at 10,741.97, up 19.90p or 0.19%, maintaining its modest gains in Friday's session despite heavy selling in US technology stocks.
The blue-chip index's resilience reflects support from large-cap companies, particularly healthcare and energy stocks.
9:00 am EDT: Futures point to weak opening on Wall Street
US stock futures are pointing to a sharply weaker opening on Friday, with Nasdaq futures leading the decline as concerns about the cost of AI investment continue to weigh on technology stocks.
At 8: 64 am EDT, technology sector looks under heavy pressure: Nasdaq futures were down 2.55% to 28,808, suggesting investors are continuing to sell growth and technology shares.
The S&P 500 was also weaker, down 1.03% to 7674, indicating that selling was spreading beyond the technology-heavy Nasdaq.
The Dow is holding up: A marginal 0.03% gain to 52,529suggests relative resilience among large established companies.
The FTSE 100 has strengthened slightly over the past hour, rising from 10,741.78, up to 10,744.44, up by 0.21%, an additional gain of 2.66p and an overall gain of about 22p.
The index is maintaining its positive momentum, although the modest increase suggests that buying interest remains measured rather than signalling a decisive rally.
Broad weakness is seen in the US dollar against most major currencies on Friday, with sterling, the euro, yen and Swiss franc all strengthening against the greenback.
The dollar was down 0.39% against the pound.
It lost 0.14% against the euro, extending the currency's recovery following the European Central Bank's decision to hold interest rates.
The dollar's weakness is particularly notable against the backdrop of stronger-than-expected US third-quarter GDP growth and accelerating September inflation, which have strengthened expectations of a possible Federal Reserve rate increase in December.
Best of the brokers
-
BP PLC (LSE:BP.) (LSE: BP.) beat Q3 earnings forecasts with underlying replacement cost net income of US$8.46bn, 15% above consensus. Jefferies maintained a Hold rating with a 550p target price, while UBS reiterated a Buy rating with a 700p target, citing stronger-than-expected operating profits across all three divisions.
-
Filtronic PLC (LSE:FTC) (LSE: FTC) shares fell 1% to 223p despite an in-line AGM update highlighting new satellite and defence opportunities. The company secured an initial US$0.3m development order for Ka-band amplifiers for GEO satellite ground stations. Cavendish reiterated its 'buy' rating and 290p target price, implying around 30% upside.
-
NatWest Group PLC (LSE:NWG) (LSE: NWG) shares dropped as much as 4% to 610.4p after Q3 results. Jefferies highlighted ongoing risks to net interest income forecasts for 2027 and 2028 but maintained its 'buy' rating and 770p target price, implying approximately 21% upside from the previous close.
12:00 noon GMT: FTSE 100 moves up
The FTSE 100 is edging higher, but weakness in mid-cap and smaller-company shares points to a divided London market.
The FTSE 100 is supported by strong gains in BT Group, AstraZeneca and several consumer-facing companies.
The FTSE 250 is underperforming sharply, falling 0.68%, suggesting weakness among domestically focused and mid-cap shares.
The AIM market is weaker still, down 0.86%, indicating that selling pressure extends into smaller companies.
FTSE 100: 10,741.78, up 19.71p (0.18%).
FTSE 250: 24,506.01, down 168.15p (0.68%).
Nasdaq futures fell more than 2% on Friday morning as Amazon's plans for continued heavy AI investment and Intel's warning of cash burn this year heightened concerns about the rising cost of AI infrastructure and the time needed to generate returns.
Amazon shares fell 6.3% in premarket trading after the company reported a sharp cash outflow in the third quarter and signalled a further increase in capital expenditure next year.
11:00 AM GMT: FTSE 100 gained ground
The London Stock Exchange emerged as an outlier of resilience among European peers by late morning, shielding itself from a severe global technology stock rout.
The FTSE 100 index of leading blue-chip companies hovered 1% higher at 10733 points.
Domestic equity markets responded constructively to corporate earnings beats and a sense of relief surrounding the newly unveiled UK budget.
AstraZeneca PLC (LSE:AZN, NYSE:AZN), the FTSE 100 pharmaceutical company, saw its shares surge 4% to £120 after posting an oncology-driven quarterly beat and detailing a comprehensive £1 billion restructuring program.
Heavyweight energy producers advanced on the back of strong refining margins, coupled with Brent crude climbing above $115 per barrel due to global energy supply anxieties.
Conversely, the FTSE 250 index of mid-cap companies traded down, slipping 1% as investors adjusted portfolios to lower domestic growth projections and higher borrowing profiles outlined in the fiscal budget.
Small-cap round up
Small-cap companies tracking the alternative investment market experienced light trading volumes but remained broadly stable, supported by targeted corporate tax exemptions preserved in the fiscal update.
-
Central Asia Metals PLC (AIM:CAML, OTC:CAMLF) disclosed a TR-1 major shareholding notification, reporting a significant change in ownership by a major investor.
-
NextEnergy Solar Fund Ltd (LSE:NESF, FRA:5NE) disclosed a regulatory Form 8.5 filing detailing share dealings and positions held by a market participant during an offer period.
-
Solvonis Therapeutics PLC (LSE:SVNS, OTC:SLVNF) announces board change as director departs.
-
Ariana Resources PLC (AIM:AAU, ASX:AA2, FRA:4A6) advances Dokwe gold project with strong drilling results and a £17.3m cash position as feasibility work gathers pace.
10:00 AM GMT: Blue chips resilient
The FTSE 100 Index (INDEXFTSE:UKX) gained 0.3% to trade at 10,722 during afternoon trading in London.
The domestic benchmark dodged a deeper downturn hitting international peers due to its structurally low exposure to megacap technology companies.
Strong corporate earnings from heavyweights AstraZeneca PLC (LSE:AZN, NYSE:AZN) and BP (LON:BP) underpinned the gains as the index headed toward its first monthly advance in three months.
A softer-than-expected UK budget statement also provided long-term support for corporate equities across the main exchange.
The medium-sized companies in the FTSE 250 Index (INDEXFTSE:MCX) held steady, trading around the 24,674 level to reflect stable domestic conditions.
Airtel Africa PLC (LSE:AAF), the telecommunications provider, drew heavy trading volume following the publication of its half-year results.
Shell PLC (LSE:SHEL, NYSE:SHEL), the energy major, supported the broader index following a major announcement to increase its fourth-quarter share buyback program to $5 billion.
Sentiment on the trading floor was further buoyed by major monetary policy updates from the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan.
The European Central Bank maintained its benchmark deposit rate at 2.5%, signalling a measured tightening stance that reassured European market participants.
Sovereign gilt yields declined across the board, providing a stable backdrop for domestic equity valuations during the afternoon session.
The British pound edged higher to trade above $1.34 against the United States dollar, reflecting localized confidence in the economic trajectory.
9.00am GMT: Blue-chips outperform
The FTSE 100 gained 40 points to 10,762, while the FTSE 250 dropped 63 points to 24,611 and the AIM All-Share lost 0.5%.
Telecoms and healthcare led the blue-chips, with BT up 4.4% and AstraZeneca gaining 2.5% after third-quarter revenue rose 7% and full-year guidance was retained.
Prudential, Experian and RELX advanced between 2.7% and 3.3%, adding support from financial and information-services shares.
Airtel Africa fell 6.6% after its results showed higher finance costs and a 115% increase in capital spending despite strong revenue growth.
NatWest dropped 3.1% after reporting flat third-quarter pre-tax profit of £2.2 billion.
Technology trusts Polar Capital Technology and Scottish Mortgage lost 4.1% and 2.6% following the Wall Street and Asian technology sell-off, while Fresnillo and Antofagasta retreated as metals weakened.
Among mid-caps, Trustpilot and Rightmove gained around 2.6%, but Ceres Power fell 7.5%.
8.15 am GMT: Blue-chips make positive start
The FTSE 100 gained 29 points to 10,752 at 8.15 am GMT after touching 10,784, while the FTSE 250 was unchanged at 24,674.
London Stock Exchange Group and Diageo rose around 1.8%, with 3i Group and ICG also edging higher.
Early trading remained selective rather than broadly risk-on, as Melrose fell 1.4%, Lloyds dropped 1.3%, and Rio Tinto slipped 1%.
The flat mid-cap index showed that the early strength was concentrated among larger companies rather than spread evenly across the market.
London resisted weaker leads from Wall Street and technology-heavy Asian markets, with financial-market and consumer shares providing support.
Results from AstraZeneca, BP, NatWest and Airtel Africa provided the main company-specific focus.
7.00 am GMT: London set for positive open
London shares are expected to open higher on Friday, with IG pricing the FTSE 100 around 42 points stronger at 10,764 after the index closed 0.3% higher at 10,722 on Thursday.
The positive London call comes despite losses on Wall Street and across technology-heavy Asian markets.
The S&P 500 declined 0.3% to 7,720, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.4% to 26,185, and the Dow Jones fell 0.3% to 52,343.
Alphabet plunged 12.6% in its worst decline for more than 20 years after weaker growth intensified concerns about whether heavy investment in artificial intelligence will generate sufficient returns.
Amazon extended the cautious technology backdrop after its shares fell around 7% in after-hours trading following an earnings miss and a subdued fourth-quarter outlook.
The Wall Street retreat spread into Asia, where Japan's Nikkei lost more than 2%, South Korea's Kospi fell sharply and Taiwan's Taiex declined more than 2% as semiconductor and technology shares came under pressure.
The Bank of Japan kept its policy rate unchanged at 1.25%, following the increase delivered in September.
Hong Kong moved against the regional trend as the Hang Seng gained about 1.7%, while the Shanghai Composite edged lower.
Australia's ASX 200 closed 0.2% higher at 8,908 after surrendering most of its early advance.
Brent crude rose about 1% to $116 a barrel, gold fell 0.6% to $4,007 and Bitcoin declined 2.2% to around $78,500.
BP, NatWest, AstraZeneca and Airtel Africa lead Friday's corporate calendar, while Nationwide house-price figures provide the early domestic economic focus.
